source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, ranking 14th in Texas, but only 19 of the state's 133 mapped facilities disclose power at all.

That gap is the real finding. Texas shows 475 MW of disclosed data center IT load, and SAT1 accounts for 1.9% of it, but the total is a floor rather than a measurement. The state's ranking behind California and Virginia rests on the same partial disclosure, so it describes what operators have chosen to publish, not what has been built. Any estimate of AI capacity in Texas that leans on these figures inherits the same blind spot.

For AI specifically, 9 MW is small. The data's own conversion, at an assumed 40 kW per rack, puts SAT1 at roughly 225 racks, which is not a training campus. The certifications for HIPAA, PCI DSS, FISMA, and ISO 27001 point to regulated workloads and smaller deployments instead. The 40 kW per rack figure is an assumption about utilization, not a published specification, and the rack count should be read that way.

What the data does not cover matters as much. Backup power, renewable sourcing, grid connection, and any announced expansion are absent, and the suitability score of 56 lists announced expansion as its missing input. Nothing here says how SAT1 is powered or whether it can grow.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
